title: Creating Your First Next.js App
description: Set up a brand new Next.js project with one command and explore the folder structure.

slides.title: Prerequisites 📋
slides.content:
# What You Need

* **Node.js** (version 18.17 or later) – download from [nodejs.org](https://nodejs.org)
* A code editor (VS Code recommended)
* Terminal / command line

We'll use `create-next-app`, the official starter tool.

slides.title: Create the App 🎉
slides.content: Run this command in your terminal. It will ask a few questions – you can press Enter to accept the defaults.

quizData.question: What does `npx` do?

options.text: Runs a package without permanently installing it

quizData.explanation: `npx` executes a command from an npm package without adding it to your global or local packages permanently.

slides.title: Project Structure Overview 📁
slides.content:
# Important Folders & Files

* `pages/` – Every file here becomes a route. This is where you put your components.
* `public/` – Static assets (images, fonts). They are served directly.
* `styles/` – CSS files (global and module CSS).
* `next.config.js` – Configuration for Next.js.
* `package.json` – Dependencies and scripts.

slides.title: The pages/index.js File
slides.content: Your homepage is `pages/index.js`. Open it and you'll see a React component.

quizData.question: Which file in the `pages/` directory automatically becomes the route `/`?
quizData.explanation: In Next.js file‑system routing, `index.js` inside a folder maps to the root of that path. `pages/index.js` → `/`.

slides.title: Don't Delete `_app.js` 🚨
slides.content: `pages/_app.js` is the custom App component. It wraps all pages. You'll need it later for global styles, layouts, and state management. Keep it safe!
